attempts.t5_prompt: A highly detailed scientific cross-section diagram showing the internal anatomy of a plant cell with all major organelles and structures precisely rendered. The rigid cellulose cell wall forms the outermost boundary, displaying its characteristic geometric lattice structure that provides structural support and rigidity to the plant cell. Directly beneath the cell wall lies the semi-permeable cell membrane which controls the passage of materials into and out of the cell. The nucleus occupies a prominent central position within the cell, containing the nucleolus and displaying the cell's genetic material organized as DNA, serving as the control center that regulates all cellular functions and gene expression. Numerous chloroplasts are distributed throughout the cytoplasm, each displaying their characteristic double membrane envelope with stacked internal thylakoid structures where photosynthesis occurs, containing chlorophyll pigments that appear green. The vacuole occupies a large central space, providing turgor pressure that maintains cell rigidity and storing water, nutrients, and pigments. Mitochondria are scattered throughout the cytoplasm, appearing as elongated structures with cristae visible in cross-section. The endoplasmic reticulum extends throughout the cytoplasm in rough and smooth varieties, with ribosomes attached to rough ER for protein synthesis. The Golgi apparatus appears as stacked membrane compartments involved in protein processing and packaging. Small vesicles and storage granules fill the remaining cytoplasmic space. The entire composition is rendered in educational scientific textbook style with accurate biological coloring, white background, no text labels, and three-dimensional cross-sectional perspective showing spatial relationships between all cellular components.
